chose: One voice policy for every essay kind (voices.ts), a union of two cases. `fixed` is one voice per speaker for the whole video: what every version before it says, byte for byte, and the weekly call's, whose sections each have their own voice already. `lanes` gives each role its own lane of Kokoro voices, disjoint from the other lanes, so two roles never share a voice. The nth chapter a role speaks in takes its lane's nth voice, round robin, so its voice holds through a chapter and changes each time it speaks in a new one, even after chapters it sat out; the same essay always gets the same voices. The host, narrator, tutor and asker have three voices each. The answerer, which stands in for the owner in a sample with no takes, holds one voice (bm_george, the sample's voice before the lanes), since the owner's own voice never changes. A spoken card's Kokoro answer is the tutor's role, as its bubble draws the tutor's bird. A chapter is what the video marks: a chapter slide in an essay, a chapter mark in a cards essay, a spoken card included. So an exchange sits within one chapter, and its asker and answerer keep their voices through it; the asker's lane is women's voices and the answerer a British man's, so the two differ by more than name. The lanes hold voices Kokoro grades C or better, and the host's and narrator's open on the voices they had, so a cards essay's intro and first card sound as before. They are turned on by a `voices: "lanes-v1"` field in a template's shape and a series, as C822 turned on the cast, so a pinned version never changes voice; the essays' locked intro says the tutor's voice changes only from those versions, so an older intro's take is unchanged. The Rust essay's version 7, the interview essay's version 4 and cheat-sheet's version 4 name the lanes, and the routine pins cheat-sheet 4. The call stays `fixed`: the lanes would rotate its host, so they don't subsume its per-section voices, and its output is unchanged. The pool is the English voices home's speaker loads (Kokoro-FastAPI v0.9.2, voices/v1_0).
options: a lane per role, disjoint, round robin over the chapters each role speaks in, the owner's stand-in held (chosen)
round robin over every chapter of the video: a role that sits out two chapters can come back in the same voice
one shared pool, each role offset by its place: a voice can pass from one role to the next across a boundary, so a listener hears the narrator become the host
random per chapter, seeded by the essay: deterministic too, but two chapters in a row can land on the same voice
rotate the call's sections too: changes a weekly call's voices that the owner already enjoys
gray: Which voices the owner hears, and where they change, is on the screen; no check settled the lanes' members or what counts as a chapter.
undo: Drop `voices` from the shapes, the series schema and cheat-sheet v4, delete rust-essay/v7.json and cheat-sheet/v4.json, set ESSAY_VERSION back to 6 and INTERVIEW_ESSAY_VERSION to 3, and the policy's `fixed` case says what every essay said before. Essays written at the newer versions are then refused (VS1).
